page_title: How To Establish a High Severity Incident Management Program

sources.entry: How To Establish a High Severity Incident Management Program

summary.name: High Severity Incident Management Program Guide
summary.one_liner: A Gremlin guide explaining how to establish and measure a high severity (SEV) incident management program, covering SEV levels, on-call roles, categorization, naming, and prevention.
keywords: how to set up incident management
use_cases: Setting up a severity classification scheme for incidents
Defining incident manager and tech lead on-call roles
Measuring incident impact against SLAs and SLOs
Training staff to log incidents company-wide
summary.what_it_does: The page is a three-part series introduction describing how to build a high severity incident (SEV) program. It defines the SEV lifecycle (detection, diagnosis, mitigation, prevention, closure) and explains SEV levels, including separate examples for free/freemium and subscription products. It covers the Incident Manager On-Call and Tech Lead On-Call roles, with training and rotation practices. It also describes measuring SEVs by availability error rate multiplied by outage duration, and gives advice on naming, categorizing, and preventing repeat incidents using postmortems and chaos engineering.
notable: Defines IMOC and TLOC on-call roles with rotation and escalation guidance
Measures SEV impact as % loss times outage duration, tied to SLA breach checks
Recommends a Google Form (RecordSEV) so all engineers can log incidents
caveats: Page is a guide, not a software product; the RecordSEV tool is a Google Form template
Example SEV level tables and diagrams are referenced but not present in the text
